result.markdown: --- title: "Forecasting Seoul's hourly bike demand" subtitle: "A leakage-safe operational case study with interpretable benchmarks" author: "Miguelangel Palma Rojas" date: last-modified lang: en description: "An end-to-end forecasting workflow for bicycle rebalancing, evaluated on a strictly future holdout." --- Hourly demand is not just a prediction problem. It is an operating decision: how many bicycles should be available, where should the team expect pressure, and how much uncertainty remains at commuter peaks? ::: {.metric-grid} ::: {.metric-card} Random forest Best final model ::: ::: {.metric-card} 319.6 bikes Holdout RMSE ::: ::: {.metric-card} 28.0% RMSE gain vs calendar baseline ::: ::: {.metric-card} 564 bikes Peak-demand MAE ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## Decision takeaway Use the winning model as a planning signal, not an autonomous dispatch rule. It materially improves the calendar benchmark, but its negative bias and larger peak error call for an operational safety buffer. ::: ## Data contract and quality The committed snapshot contains 8,760 hourly observations from 2017-12-01 through 2018-11-30. The pipeline validates schema, completeness, physical ranges, nonnegative rentals, and unique date-hour keys before modeling. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bikes <- read_bike_snapshot() bike_data_profile(bikes) |> kable(digits = 1, caption = "Validated snapshot profile") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Validated snapshot profile | observations|first_date |last_date | operating_days| closure_hours| average_hourly_demand| peak_hourly_demand| missing_cells| |------------:|:----------|:----------|--------------:|-------------:|---------------------:|------------------:|-------------:| | 8760|2017-12-01 |2018-11-30 | 353| 295| 704.6| 3556| 0| ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_demand_heatmap(bikes, "en") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Average operating-day rentals by weekday and hour.](index_files/figure-html/demand-rhythm-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Forecast design The last 20% of complete dates is untouched until the final comparison. Hyperparameters are selected with expanding temporal windows; every validation window follows its training window and a one-day gap reduces boundary leakage. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} model_data <- prepare_modeling_data(bikes) partition <- temporal_partition(model_data, test_fraction = 0.20) resamples <- temporal_resamples( partition$training, folds = 4, assessment_days = 28, gap_days = 1 ) temporal_window_summary(list(resamples = resamples)) |> kable(caption = "Expanding validation windows") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Expanding validation windows |window |training_start |training_end |validation_start |validation_end | training_rows| validation_rows| |:--------|:--------------|:------------|:----------------|:--------------|-------------:|---------------:| |Window01 |2017-12-01 |2018-04-05 |2018-04-07 |2018-05-05 | 3024| 672| |Window02 |2017-12-01 |2018-05-19 |2018-05-21 |2018-06-17 | 4032| 672| |Window03 |2017-12-01 |2018-07-01 |2018-07-03 |2018-07-30 | 5064| 672| |Window04 |2017-12-01 |2018-08-12 |2018-08-14 |2018-09-10 | 6072| 672| ::: ::: The recipe treats date as an identifier, encodes categorical calendar signals, removes zero-variance and linearly dependent columns, and normalizes numeric predictors. Four candidates make the result auditable: a weekday-hour benchmark, ordinary linear regression, Elastic Net, and random forest. Independent fixed seeds govern each search grid and the random-forest engine, so both language editions reproduce the same result. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} recipe <- bike_recipe(partition$training) forest_spec <- rand_forest( mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 300 ) |> set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") |> set_mode("regression") workflow() |> add_recipe(recipe) |> add_model(forest_spec) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` == Workflow ==================================================================== Preprocessor: Recipe Model: rand_forest() -- Preprocessor ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6 Recipe Steps * step_unknown() * step_novel() * step_dummy() * step_zv() * step_lincomb() * step_normalize() -- Model ----------------------------------------------------------------------- Random Forest Model Specification (regression) Main Arguments: mtry = tune() trees = 300 min_n = tune() Engine-Specific Arguments: importance = permutation Computational engine: ranger ``` ::: ::: ## Final holdout results ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} results$metrics |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))) |> kable(caption = "Operational metrics on unseen future dates") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Operational metrics on unseen future dates |model | rmse| mae| rsq| wape_pct| bias| peak_mae| |:-----------------|-----:|-----:|---:|--------:|------:|--------:| |Random forest | 319.6| 225.9| 0.7| 25.2| -55.5| 564.0| |Elastic Net | 365.1| 268.6| 0.6| 30.0| -77.7| 713.6| |Linear regression | 414.0| 321.5| 0.5| 35.9| -204.1| 784.5| |Calendar baseline | 444.0| 323.7| 0.5| 36.2| -206.5| 866.4| ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_model_metrics(results$metrics, "en") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Lower RMSE is better; evaluation uses only the final future holdout.](index_files/figure-html/model-comparison-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: RMSE penalizes large misses, MAE describes the typical absolute miss, WAPE expresses total error relative to observed demand, bias shows systematic over- or under-forecasting, and peak MAE isolates the busiest 10% of training demand. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_holdout_series(results, language = "en") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Observed demand and the winning model over the final seven days.](index_files/figure-html/holdout-trace-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Operational diagnostics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_peak_residuals(results, "en") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Positive residuals indicate under-forecasting.](index_files/figure-html/peak-errors-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_variable_importance(results$importance, "en") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Permutation importance describes predictive contribution, not causality.](index_files/figure-html/feature-importance-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Temperature, trend, moisture conditions, solar radiation, and commute-hour indicators carry much of the signal. This does not make them causal levers; it makes them useful forecasting inputs. ## From forecast to action - Refresh the forecast before each operating shift with the latest weather outlook. - Convert expected rentals into station-level targets only after adding station inventory and trip-flow data. - Add a peak buffer when the cost of stockouts exceeds the cost of carrying idle bicycles. - Monitor WAPE, bias, and peak MAE by season; retrain when performance drifts beyond agreed thresholds. - Keep closures outside the demand model and handle them with an explicit service-status rule. The dataset covers one year and has no station, capacity, pricing, event, or forecast-weather fields. The result demonstrates sound model evaluation, but it is not yet a production rebalancing system. See the [methodology](docs/methodology.md), [model card](docs/model-card.md), and [data dictionary](docs/data-dictionary.md) for the complete audit trail.
